residents.name: Grandmother Cap's ring
residents.kind: a named Pokemon with a trap for a trigger: the folk tale is the warning
residents.situation: On the flat mushroom heath of the Fungal Isle's south half stands a perfect ring of red-and-white toadstools, ten blocks across, on a band of dark podzol. Inside it sit three more, small, and one big one. Islanders and ferry crews leave the ring alone, and someone has put up signs to say so. The big one is Grandmother Cap, an old Amoonguss who has sat in the middle of her own decoys for as long as anyone has rowed past. She is asleep until somebody steps over the ring: the trigger is the ring itself (trigger 9 against the ring's radius of 10), so the warning on the sign is exactly the rule.

residents.name: Post Fourteen and Ash
residents.kind: a named Pokemon left behind, its story told by the place alone: signs, a worn track, an empty post
residents.situation: On the flat top of Long Isle's north end stands a Haven Compact field post: a timber hut, a watchtower, and twenty blocks east of them a ring of smooth stone in the turf with a plank bar laid across it, the Compact's own field symbol (docs/story/FACTION.md: 'a plain open ring crossed by a short bridge'), and in its middle the stump of a field anchor (FACTION.md 'Method' 3: anchors define an exchange boundary). The crew went one night and did not come back. The sign by the door says relief was due in three days. The other says 'ASH: stay. guard. good dog. back soon.' Round the hut runs a perfect ring of bare trodden earth twenty-eight blocks across: Ash is a Houndoom and has walked that circuit every night since. Ash sleeps on the porch until someone comes within twenty blocks, and will not leave the post. Catching Ash is the only ending the place offers, and the only reward: somebody finally comes back.
residents.story_rule: nothing here says where the crew went, why, or what the anchor was for: the signs say only what a sergeant would write on a door. The arc's facts stay in docs/story/ (FACTION.md 'Method'); this place is consistent with them and reveals nothing they do not. Tier 7 and gated after gym 7, by when the player has met the Compact (docs/story/ARC.md, gym2_town)

residents.name: Tobiah Rusk's half-house
residents.kind: a story beat with nothing to fetch: one man, one strange fact, one question he asks you
residents.situation: In the open middle of Sunset Isle stands half a cottage. The west half is all there: walls, a gable roof, a door with a nameplate for two, a cold hearth, a bedroll, a lantern on a chain. The east half is not, and never fell down: the floorboards, the table, the rug and the roof all stop on one straight line, and the line goes on out of the house, a scar of bare earth and gravel running due north and south across the meadow for a hundred and twenty-nine blocks. Tobiah Rusk lives in the half that stayed. His wife Nell was in the kitchen, and the kitchen was on the other side of the line. He sets her place every night, and he will ask you one thing.
residents.story_rule: Tobiah does not know what an exchange is and never says the word; he says what he saw (a white light that stood along one line) and what he believes (a cut that clean moves people). That is the evidence every exchanged edge shows (docs/story/ARC.md, Pallet's 'localized damage where the exchange boundary closed badly'; docs/story/FACTION.md 'Method'), and nothing more. Sunset Isle is tier 8 (sunset_east), reached by the ferry, long after the player has heard the native account of displacement at gym1_town

residents.name: Corran Vey's survey line
residents.kind: a fetch with a reason: something the player makes, for a man whose instrument stopped working
residents.situation: On the slope above Sunset Isle's north beach is a surveyor's camp: a canvas tent, a theodolite on its tripod, a cartography table, a field book on a lectern, a cut datum stone with his initials. From it a line of red-and-white ranging poles runs dead straight, one every eight paces, bearing thirty degrees east of north, down the meadow, across the sand, and on into the sea, the poles standing in the water as far as it is shallow enough to set one. Corran Vey has chained this line four hundred miles from somewhere else, and it walks into the strait. His compass came with him and will not settle. He wants one made here: a compass is four iron and a redstone at any crafting table, and he takes it, takes a bearing, and gives the player his datum stone, an Everstone, because nothing ever changed it and everything around it did.
residents.story_rule: Corran says what a surveyor would see (the land does not match his plan; his old compass will not settle) and believes a compass made here will. Nothing in Minecraft makes his old compass spin; he says it does, and the dialogue never claims more than that the new one points the same way twice. Sunset Isle west is tier 5 (sunset_west), reached by the Sunset strait ferry (data/ferry_docks.json sunset_isle_landing)

residents.name: Bettany Oake's last claim
residents.kind: directions to a place: she cannot climb to it any more, and tells you how to find it
residents.situation: On the open upland of the Arrow Creeks an old prospector keeps a lean-to with a sluice, a grindstone, a basin for panning and a fire. Bettany Oake worked the creeks for forty years, until one spring half of them came down the other side of the hill. Her best claim, Number Four, was up where the old creek bed ran; her knees will not take her up there now. She tells the player the way in words only: into the sunset, uphill, until the ground stops rising. About a hundred and ninety blocks west-north-west, on the crest, stands her cairn with her pick still in it, and in the barrel set in the ground at its foot is what she put by.
residents.story_rule: the creeks moving is what Bettany saw and nothing more; she does not know why, and says nobody asked her. The Arrow Creeks are tier 8, a late, remote upland; the find is sized to that (data/rewards.json prospector_claim)

residents.name: Hale Brannock's bench
residents.kind: a beat gated on the player's own progress: he has waited thirty-one years for someone to bring him the eighth badge
residents.situation: Out on the open plain east of Holdfast, on a rise from which the gatehouse of the Holdfast gym shows on the western skyline, an old man has put a bench, two lanterns, a fire, and behind the bench a board with eight slots. Seven hold a badge's colours (Boulder, Cascade, Thunder, Rainbow, Soul, Marsh, Volcano); the eighth is a hole straight through the board. Hale Brannock walked up to that gate thirty-one years ago with seven badges and came back down the same road. The Holdfast gym is the Gate of the South (data/gym_buildings/gym8.json: 'for seven badges it is the building everyone walks past, and for the eighth it is the one you have to go through to leave'). He will talk to anyone; when the player has cleared gym 8 he asks to see the badge, and gives them the Leftovers his Snorlax carried through every fight they had, so that it goes through the gate.
residents.story_rule: the gym's leader thirty-one years ago is never named: Hale says 'that gate', never a person. The badge names are the Kanto badges our eight leaders give (data/towns.json leaders; CobbleverseBadges). The option to show the badge reads the progression flag gym8_cleared (compile_dialogue's flag probe, the ferry's proven shape), not a badge item
